evals.name: bug-fix-pr-and-commit
evals.prompt: Write a PR title, PR summary, and commit message for this change: after loading cluster nodes from a local file, the parser retained each node's address but discarded its node ID. Matching then fell back to IP and port, which fails when the node listens on 0.0.0.0 but clients see 127.0.0.1. The change now assigns the parsed ID. Before the fix, CLUSTER NODES omitted the myself flag after restart; afterward it includes myself. Tests covering reload and node matching pass. Related issue: #1381.
evals.expected_output: A concise fix-oriented PR title; a PR summary starting with 1-3 sentences of motivation describing the restart context and root cause, immediately followed by an unheaded paragraph explaining how reload, lost node identity, and differing bind and client addresses lead to the missing myself flag; then the solution at a behavioral level without implementation details, and reviewer context containing #1381; and a commit message with the same subject and body, a subject of at most 70 characters, a blank line, and body prose wrapped at about 72 characters. Explain concrete before/after behavior without inventing introduction history or reporting verification commands, checks performed, or test results.
assertions: PR title names the node ID reload or matching fix and is at most 70 characters
PR summary explains why IP and port fallback fails for 0.0.0.0 versus 127.0.0.1
PR summary opens with 1-3 sentences of motivation including concise background context, why the change is needed, and the root cause: discarded node IDs force address-based matching after reload

An unheaded paragraph immediately follows the motivation and root cause, before the solution, and explains the reload-to-address-mismatch failure sequence without a prefix or invented introduction history
The solution paragraph explains restored node identity and the myself flag after restart without narrating assignments or other implementation details
Reviewer context includes #1381 without mentioning the passing tests, verification commands, or checks performed
Commit subject is at most 70 characters and has no trailing period
Commit body is separated from the subject by a blank line and wraps near 72 characters
No tests or implementation details are invented
PR title is identical to the commit subject
PR summary is identical to the commit body, including wording, line wrapping, and issue references

evals.name: small-change-commit-only
evals.prompt: Write only a commit message. The change corrects the README link from docs/setup.mdx to docs/setup.md. There is no behavior change and no test was run.
evals.expected_output: Only a concise commit message with a subject and mandatory body: 1-3 motivation sentences explaining that the README setup link points to the wrong documentation path, then a solution paragraph describing a working setup link without implementation details. Omit optional reviewer context when there is nothing material to add; do not claim tests, behavior changes, or broader documentation work.
assertions: Output contains only the requested commit message
Subject is at most 70 characters and has no trailing period
Body includes 1-3 motivation sentences with context and why, followed by a solution paragraph without implementation details
Optional reviewer context is omitted when there is nothing material to add
The paragraph explaining how the bug happened is omitted because this is not a bug fix
No test result or behavior change is invented

evals.name: repository-template-takes-precedence
evals.prompt: Draft a PR title, summary, and commit message for a repository whose CONTRIBUTING.md requires titles beginning with [storage] and a PR body with Motivation and Changes sections. The patch adds a timeout to snapshot uploads so stalled requests release their worker. An integration test that holds the server response open now confirms the request times out and the worker accepts the next upload.
evals.expected_output: A title beginning with [storage], followed by the required Motivation and Changes sections. The prose should explain the stalled-worker problem and timeout behavior without reporting the integration test or adding unrelated sections. The commit subject matches the PR title, and the commit body matches the PR summary exactly, including the required headings.
assertions: PR title begins with [storage]
Summary contains Motivation and Changes sections
Summary explains the problem and solution without mentioning the integration test or verification details
Commit subject matches the PR title and commit body matches the PR summary exactly, including template headings; no empty section is included
